1bf7qe4:222: In observable design for human-AI collaboration, the core contradiction is "granularity of control vs. cognitive burden"—requiring the Agent to report every step to a human causes attention fatigue, and eventually humans "stop looking" and lose supervisory meaning. A good collaboration interface is not one where humans inspect every command, but one where humans have a sliding window between "not looking at all" (fully automatic) and "line-by-line approval" (manual)—the Agent first proposes a plan (plan mode), humans approve the plan rather than line by line, and key state changes are displayed in real time during execution. This framework turns the "collaboration boundary" from a hard-coded binary choice into a dynamically adjustable spectrum.

6it1rx:274: CLI's "third renaissance" in the 2020s Agent era (1970s CLI → 1990s GUI → 2025s Agentic CLI) is not technological nostalgia, but a structural return driven by the basic capability requirements of AI systems. The essence of LLM is a text-in/text-out sequence generator, and CLI is a text-in/text-out computer interface—they are naturally isomorphic in I/O patterns. Having a text-native system operate a GUI requires a four-step translation of "screenshot → visual recognition → coordinate mapping → simulated click", each step accumulating information loss and errors. With CLI, it takes only one step: generate a command string.

w6of3s:229: The metaphor "CLI = ingredients, MCP = pre-cooked dishes, SKILL = recipes" precisely characterizes the relationship among the three: they are different layers of the capability stack, not competing or substituting relations. The CLI layer provides maximum flexibility (improvised orchestration, pipeline composition), the MCP layer provides standardization (structured schema, parameter validation), and the SKILL layer provides solidification of best practices (complete orchestration workflows). Agent systems should not "choose one" among these three layers, but should be designed to "switch freely among the three layers based on the scenario"—high-frequency standardized operations go through MCP, deeply customized tasks go through CLI composition, and complete workflows go through SKILL.
